per.err.perm: Could not save. Reload the page and try again.
per.m.atr.h: Concentrated blocks: accumulate a base, transform it into specific work, realize it in competition. The most common model in team sports.
per.m.linear.h: From high volume and low intensity to the opposite, as a ramp. Simple and predictable; it loses its edge when you compete often.
per.m.undulating.h: Qualities rotate within the same week instead of across blocks. It fits a calendar with a match every week.
per.m.conjugate.h: Everything is trained all the time and what rotates is the emphasis. It asks for an experienced athlete and tight load control.
per.m.free.h: You name the stages yourself, with no preset types.
per.k.accumulation.h: High volume and general work: building the base that gets transformed later.
per.k.transformation.h: Volume drops and specificity rises: the base turns into work that looks like competing.
per.k.realization.h: Low load and plenty of freshness: the stage where you compete.
per.k.transition.h: Unloading and recovery between blocks or at the close of the season.
per.k.hypertrophy.h: Long sets and high volume to gain muscle mass.
per.k.strength.h: Heavy loads and few reps to gain maximal strength.
per.k.power.h: Moderate loads moved fast: the strength gained becomes speed.
per.k.deload.h: A deliberately easy week, so the body absorbs what came before.
per.k.high.h: The hard days of the week.
per.k.medium.h: Sustained work, short of the limit.
per.k.max_effort.h: Near-maximal loads for very few reps.
per.k.dynamic_effort.h: Light loads moved at top speed.
per.k.repetition.h: Accessory volume to pile up work without taxing the nervous system.

as.title: Their tests
as.none: No tests yet. With three takes of the same test you can already compare today against their own level.
as.needMore: {n} more take to compare|{n} more takes to compare
as.errNum: The result has to be a number.
as.errRange: For this test a value between {min} and {max} {u} is expected. Check the number.
as.errSave: Could not save. Reload the page and try again.
as.t.cmj.h: Standing, hands on hips: dip and jump in one motion, as high as possible. Best of three, a minute between jumps. This is the one that warns best when the nervous system has not recovered.
as.t.sj.h: Same as the previous one but starting still, knees already bent and no dip before jumping. Compared with the other one it says how much they use the rebound.
as.t.slcmj.h: The same jump standing on one leg, without help from the other. What matters here is the difference between sides.
as.t.broad_jump.h: Feet together, jump forward as far as possible and land stable. Measured from the start line to the rearmost heel. All you need is a tape measure.
as.t.triple_hop.h: Three hops in a row on the same leg, without stopping in between. Total distance is measured. Widely used to see how a leg is doing after an injury.
as.t.sprint.h: One single run, from a standing start whenever they are ready, filmed on the phone. Write down the cumulative time at each distance. The profile comes out of those splits: how much force they can put into the ground and how fast they can go. The 10 m and the 30 m on their own do not tell apart an athlete who pushes hard and fades from one who starts slow and flies at the end.
as.t.cod_505.h: Run 10 m, brake, turn on one leg and come back 5 m. The last 5 m out and the 5 m back are timed. Taken turning on each leg: the difference between sides is the point.
as.t.pushups.h: As many as possible in a row, without stopping, chest reaching a fist off the floor. Write down how many.
as.t.plank.h: Face down on the forearms, body in line. It ends when the hips drop or rise. Write down the seconds.
as.t.side_plank.h: On one forearm, hips up and in line. Taken on both sides and compared.
as.t.calf_raise.h: Standing on one leg, rise onto the toes and come down at an even rhythm. Count the reps until they no longer reach the top.
as.t.cooper.h: Run for twelve minutes and note the metres covered. The phone's GPS is enough. Flat ground and, if repeated, the same route.
as.t.run_1000.h: A thousand metres as fast as possible, on the flat. Note the time in seconds.
as.t.sit_reach.h: Seated with legs straight, take the hands towards the feet without bouncing. Measured from the sole of the foot: past it is positive, short of it is negative.
as.t.ankle_lunge.h: Kneeling in front of a wall, take the knee to touch the wall without lifting the heel. Measure how far the foot can be moved back. Taken on both sides.
as.t.rhr.h: Just awake, before getting out of bed, count the beats for one minute. It rises while the body is still recovering: it is the cheapest signal there is.
as.r.samozino: Samozino P, Rabita G, Dorel S, Slawinski J, Peyrot N, Saez de Villarreal E, Morin JB (2016). A simple method for measuring power, force, velocity properties, and mechanical effectiveness in sprint running. Scand J Med Sci Sports 26(6):648–658. · Validado con teléfono: Romero-Franco N et al. (2017), Eur J Sport Sci 17(4):386–392.
as.r.cmj: Balsalobre-Fernández C, Glaister M, Lockey RA (2015). The validity and reliability of an iPhone app for measuring vertical jump performance. J Sports Sci 33(15):1574–1579. · Altura por tiempo de vuelo: Bosco C, Luhtanen P, Komi PV (1983), Eur J Appl Physiol 50(2):273–282. · Como marcador de fatiga: Claudino JG et al. (2017), J Sci Med Sport 20(4):397–402.
as.r.myjump: Balsalobre-Fernández C, Glaister M, Lockey RA (2015). The validity and reliability of an iPhone app for measuring vertical jump performance. J Sports Sci 33(15):1574–1579.
as.r.hop: Noyes FR, Barber SD, Mangine RE (1991). Abnormal lower limb symmetry determined by function hop tests after anterior cruciate ligament rupture. Am J Sports Med 19(5):513–518.
as.r.cod: Nimphius S, Callaghan SJ, Bezodis NE, Lockie RG (2018). Change of direction and agility tests: challenging our current measures of performance. Strength Cond J 40(1):26–38.
as.r.cooper: Cooper KH (1968). A means of assessing maximal oxygen intake: correlation between field and treadmill testing. JAMA 203(3):201–204.
as.sp.hint: Times are cumulative from the start. With four or more the profile comes out; with fewer, only the segment speeds.
as.sp.f0.h: F0: the horizontal force they could apply at zero speed. That is the start, the first metres.
as.sp.v0.h: V0: the theoretical speed at which they can no longer apply force. That is the ceiling.
as.sp.pmax.h: Pmax: maximal power, which comes from the other two (F0·V0/4).
as.sp.rfmax.h: RFmax: how much of all the force they produce goes forward rather than into the ground. That is running technique, not engine.
as.sp.drf.h: DRF: how much that orientation is lost as speed builds. Less negative is better.
as.sp.needSplits: {n} more split is needed to work out the profile.|{n} more splits are needed to work out the profile.
as.sp.needWeight: The athlete's weight is missing to work out the profile.
as.sp.needHeight: The athlete's height is missing to work out the profile.
as.sp.meanwhile: In the meantime, the fastest segment was at {v} km/h.
as.sp.badFit: The splits do not fit a single run: the model sits {e} cm away from the times entered. Check the timing, because a badly taken split does not make the profile worse, it makes it different.
as.errOrder: The time at {b} m has to be greater than the one at {a} m.
